newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown says has not hit business.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown says has not hit business.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said his first budget would help to get the economy back to balance and it had not "hit" business.
"I don't think it is true to say that we have hit business," he told BBC television.

"I have cut corporation tax, I have cut the tax rate for small businesses. These are big changes that give us the lowest tax rates of any competitor country that is comparable to us -- the lowest rate of corporation tax in our history."
Brown said he had tightened fiscal policy and some of his decisions had been tough, but they had been the right thing to do.

"I don't want a situation where we've got a service and consumer economy on the one hand that is expanding too much and an industrial and exporting economy that is being held back. We've got to get it back to balance and that's what I've done."

Asked if he should not have done more to take the heat out of consumption, Brown said he had taken two measures to counter rapid increases in house prices -- raising stamp duty on expensive properties and cutting mortgage interest tax relief.

"I think most people understand that that is a way of cooling down the housing market," Brown said, adding that he would not allow the housing market to get out of control as it had in the late 1980s.

When the interviewer suggested that official interest rates might rise again after next week's Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting, the Chancellor replied: "That is a decision for the Bank of England."
